metrics_overview.en: This table compares how well different machine learning models predict the target value (HPR) using various metrics. Compared to other models like RF (R²=0.7756) and XGBoost (R²=0.7495), KNN performs significantly better. The lower the RMSE (Root Mean Square Error) and MSE (Mean Squared Error), the better the model, and KNN has the lowest values (RMSE=0.1132, MSE=0.01281). Therefore, KNN is the recommended model for predicting HPR. A practical caution is that while KNN performs best on this test set, its performance might vary when applied to real-world data that differs significantly from the training data.

fig5_model_comparison.en: This chart compares how well different predictive models estimate the Hydrogen Production Rate (HPR). The models tested include KNN, RF, XGBoost, SVM, and DT. The key metric here is R² (R-squared), which measures how much of the variation in HPR is explained by the model; a value closer to 1 is better. Based on the results, the KNN model performed the best, achieving an R² of 0.8172, which is significantly higher than the next best model, RF (R²=0.7756). This suggests that KNN is the most reliable tool for predicting HPR using the available data. However, it is important to remember that model performance depends heavily on the quality and relevance of the input data, so these predictions should be used as strong guidance, not absolute facts.

fig6ab_mse_r2_features.en: This chart, titled 'MSE and R² vs feature count,' helps us understand how adding more information (features) affects the accuracy of our predictions. The R² score measures how well our model explains the variation in the data, with higher values being better, and the MSE (Mean Squared Error) measures the average squared difference between predicted and actual values, with lower values being better. Overall, the KNN model performed best, achieving an R² of 0.817 and an MSE of 0.0128, especially when using 9 features (VFA, Butyrate, Acetate, VSS, Propionate, Ethanol, COD-O, pH, and ORP_Low). This suggests that while adding features generally improves performance up to a certain point, the optimal balance was found with 9 features for KNN. A practical caution is that while KNN performed best at 9 features, other models like RF and XGBoost showed strong performance with more features (11 features for RF), suggesting that the best feature set might depend on the specific model used.
